$comment: Entity record shapes, generated by scripts/export_records_schema.py from prism's verified record models; do not edit. Every property is optional and nullable and every object allows unknown fields, because dsp-backend forwards prism's raw rows. `x-flex-list` marks a list that may arrive as a bare scalar or null: an SDK normalises it to a list (null -> [], scalar -> [scalar]). `id` is the public id.

CompanyRecord.description:
A company row, the nested ``company`` of a person row, or (the flat
subset up to ``linkedin_url``) the employer firmographics inlined onto a
person row — see :class:`PersonRecord`. Field-for-field,
``project_lookup_company()``.

id.description: The public id: the one search gives this record, and a lookup key.

Deal.description: An acquisition the company made (``acquisitions``) or suffered (``acquired_by``).

EmployeeRange.description: ``{"min", "max"}`` — either side may be absent, never both.

EmploymentEntry.description: One job the person holds or held. ``is_primary`` marks the current one.

FundingCompanyProfile.description:
Enrichment, not identity — eleven fields, all heavy per row (`bulk`
in the catalog; request `fields: ["*"]` to receive it).

id.description: The public id: the one search gives this record, and a lookup key.

GlobalPresence.description:
The countries a company employs in, from per-country headcount.

Lowercase ISO3 codes, largest headcount first. ``hq_country`` is ``None``
when the HQ country name has no ISO3 entry in the filter's name table.

NewsCompanyLinks.description:
Grouped by how the association to the article was made — both
groups are real links (`direct_link`, `linked`). The NER `name_match`
signal (dominated by stock-phrase false positives) is used to rank the
`startups` filter but never returned as output.

Organisation.description: A parent or subsidiary, with the relationship's type (``Parent``, ``Subsidiary``).

PersonRecord.description:
A person row. Employer firmographics are merged inline — the same
concepts as :class:`CompanyRecord`, ``account_``-prefixed (or, for name
and LinkedIn URL, under ``company_linkedin_url``) rather than nested,
matching the flat shape ``_project_person()`` has always emitted. Those
flat keys are kept exactly as they were, so no existing caller of these
routes changes; they are now filled from the person's parent company
instead of the thin stub in the job history. The complete parent record
also arrives, nested, as ``company`` (``None`` when the parent document is
missing). New callers should read ``company``; the flat employer keys are
the older, deprecated way to the same facts.

cmp_id.description: The employer's id, as on search hits (dsp-backend copies `company_id`).

RevenueRange.description: ``{"min", "max"}`` annual revenue band; either side may be absent.
